reference.title: Dumbbell Lying on Floor Chest Press
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale as you press up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s down, 0.4 s pause on the floor, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-1-1-0 (2 s down, 1 s pause on the floor, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: Add reps to the top of the range, then the next dumbbell (1-2.5 kg per hand).

cues.text: Lie on the mat, knees bent and feet flat; dumbbells pressed up over the chest, palms toward the feet, shoulder blades back and down.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells with the elbows about 45 degrees out from the sides, forearms vertical.
Upper arms rest on the floor for a moment; dumbbells beside the chest.
Breathe out and press up and slightly in until the arms are straight.
Dumbbells a few centimetres apart over the chest, then go again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flared straight out at 90 degrees
mistakes.fix: Bring the elbows to about 45 degrees from the body so the upper arms land on the floor angled toward the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing the elbows off the floor
mistakes.fix: Touch the floor softly, pause for a moment, then press.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bent back, dumbbells drifting toward the face
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms vertical and the wrists straight.

mistakes.mistake: Bridging the hips up to press
mistakes.fix: Keep the glutes on the floor; drive through the feet only to brace.
Press up and slightly in, stopping a few centimetres apart.

kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; at the bottom the upper arms rest on the floor with the elbows at about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow flare (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 45 degrees from the body when the upper arm touches the floor (clinical opinion)

Shorter than a bench press: the floor stops the elbows about level with the back. Bench press 1RM rose as the range was shortened, mainly by avoiding the sticking region (Martínez-Cava 2019, Smith machine)
Back of the upper arm rests briefly on the floor at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees bent about 70-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
About 2 s down, a short pause with the arms on the floor, 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #366812, Dumbbell Lying on Floor Chest Press, video (movement reference)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

Martínez-Cava, Morán-Navarro, Hernández-Belmonte, Courel-Ibáñez, Conesa-Ros, González-Badillo and Pallarés 2019, range of motion and sticking region effects on the bench press load-velocity relationship (J Sports Sci Med 18(4):645-652)
Welsch, Bird and Mayhew 2005, electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid muscles during three upper-body lifts (J Strength Cond Res 19(2):449-452)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit with the dumbbells on the thighs, roll back with them held at the chest, and at the end of the set roll them back onto the thighs rather than dropping them beside the head (clinical opinion).
Let the upper arms touch the floor softly; do not bang the elbows down or bounce off the floor.
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: neutral grip (palms facing each other) and elbows tucked closer.
Lower back discomfort: bring the feet a little closer to the hips.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher (horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm). The floor stops the elbows at about body level, so the stretched bottom of a bench press is left out (clinical opinion); with dumbbells, pectoralis activity matched barbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher (horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm). The floor stops the elbows at about body level, so the stretched bottom of a bench press is left out (clinical opinion); with dumbbells, pectoralis activity matched barbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows; with the range shortened to the upper part, the lockout share is relatively larger (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows; with the range shortened to the upper part, the lockout share is relatively larger (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Stabilises the elbow; biceps activity rose with the stability demand and was highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Stabilises the elbow; biceps activity rose with the stability demand and was highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the dumbbells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the dumbbells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the floor.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the floor.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the back flat on the floor.
